text:
maria: Heads up — we need a concrete plan for quota-driven sampling + routing when customers hit debug/inspect requests. Legal wants clear PII handling before we enable per-tenant inspect.

dan: Agreed. rough idea: keep normal telemetry sampling as-is, but when inspect is requested (canary or breakglass) we switch to a separate inspect budget that’s rate-limited per-tenant. sampled items get a `sample_reason` tag.

maria: +1. also need to ensure the console shows remaining inspect budget and recent inspect events (only metadata unless scrubbing approved). UX should make it obvious who approved the inspect.

kevin: Question: how do we avoid cross-tenant correlation if we keep hashed IDs in logs? ops/legal worried about re-identification across tenants.

dan: Use HMAC with a per-tenant salt. storage: store only the HMACed fingerprint and a short pseudo-id, not the raw id. key rotation: rotate tenant salts periodically and re-hash new data only.

kevin: Can you sketch the log envelope we’d emit? not full PII, just shape.

dan: Sure — example snippet:```json
{"envelope_version":"v2","tenant_id":"t-xxxx (internal)","sample_reason":"inspect:breakglass","fingerprint":"hmac-v1:abcd...","fields":["route","latency_ms","truncated_resp_summary"]}
```

sre-jen: For compliance we also need an audit trail that records who toggled inspect and the approval token. That should live in our audit ledger (immutable). ops people should not be able to delete it.

maria: Agreed. Flow proposal: ops requests inspect -> owner or SRE approves in console -> system attaches `approval_id` to inspect logs and increments tenant inspect budget. UI shows grantor, timestamp, TTL.

kevin: Edgecase: attachments / embeddings in responses — those can leak. We should block full-attachment capture by default unless explicitly allowed and logged as an elevated approval.

dan: Implementation detail: mark payloads with `sensitivity_level` (low|medium|high). High => strip/pseudonymize before persisting. Medium => truncate first N chars + hash. Low => keep. Mapping controlled by route config.

sre-jen: Operationally, we need a emergency-override path for oncall (breakglass) that still emits an immutable event and consumes the same inspect budget but flags the event as emergency. Also automatic email to compliance.

ops-bot: NOTE: canary rollout for per-tenant inspect budgets scheduled for 2024-09-10 02:00 UTC. Watch for budget exhaustion alerts (:bell:).

maria: UX ask: console needs an obvious red indicator when bucket < 10% and a one-click expiring request (send to owner) to ask for temporary increase. Also show recent approvers and audit links.

kevin: Security ask: do not include raw user identifiers in logs. If a developer needs raw data for a ticket, require an SRE-owner mediated export, logged in the same ledger.

dan: I'll put together a short RFC with: sampling states (normal/canary/inspect/emergency), envelope shape, HMAC rules, UI wireframes for budget display, and a runbook for exhausted budgets.

maria: Thanks. please cc compliance and security on the RFC. We should aim to land the initial phase behind a flag so we can test with 2 tenants first. :thumbsup:

kevin: One more: include a TTL on sampled entries (auto-delete after X days) unless marked for legal hold. That reduces long-term exposure.

dan: noted. will include TTL + legal-hold API.

sre-jen: Great progress. If dan posts the RFC link here I’ll schedule a quick ops review next week.

dan: RFC incoming in ~2 hours: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/r/inspect-sampling-v1 — feedback welcome.
